newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS - HK stocks left vulnerable after selloff.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK stocks left vulnerable after selloff.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chip stocks, left battered and vulnerable on Tuesday after suffering their biggest point drop since March 1996, may see more downside if interest rates remain high to defend the Hong Kong dollar.
"At the moment the key is the stability of the Hong Kong dollar," said W.I. Carr regional technical analyst Ted Chen.

"I can see a range between HK$7.73 to HK$7.76 on the spot and I know the Hong Kong Monetary Authority likes it to be under HK$7.75. A higher HIBOR rate is going to last for at least a couple more weeks, and that will put pressure on the stock market," he said.
The Hong Kong dollar has been pegged at HK$7.8 per US$1.00 since 1983 but regional currency weakness has sparked fears that the Hong Kong currency could be the next target of speculators.

One-month HIBOR (Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate) was quoted at 11.17308 percent at midday Tuesday. The interbank overnight rate soared to 18.00/20.00 percent in early trade before edging down to 10.00/12.00 percent.
As interbank rates surged, Hong Kong share prices went into a tailspin. Share prices in Bangkok and Jakarta were also hit by currency woes on Tuesday.
The Hang Seng Index dropped 619.62 points, or 3.85 percent, to 15,477.26, its biggest point decline since March 11, 1996 and its fifth largest point drop ever.
Analysts said the local dollar was not likely to crumble, but added the market still remained nervous.
"The Hong Kong dollar really is secure but that does not mean to say that people can't find a reason to speculate against it or hedge," said South China Holdings vice chairman Howard Gorges.

"There is not a fundamental argument that Hong Kong does have to devalue its currency but because there has been turmoil and some funds have become exposed in Hong Kong, there may be more than usual pressure to speculate or hedge."
The Hong Kong dollar weakened to HK$7.7430 at one point on Tuesday compared with an opening level of HK$7.7400 before strengthening to HK$7.7385/95 by Tuesday's close.
While currency markets remained unstable, analysts said stocks were also likely to be volatile.

"I don't expect the market to have significant downside but it could still test 15,300 to 15,000 tomorrow. Today the selling in the Hang Seng Index was quite serious and I don't expect those stocks to recover suddenly," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
"I think the Hong Kong government is strong enough to protect the currency but I think the currency will be quite volatile," he added.
Heavy losses in Wall Street stocks last week also contributed to Tuesday's decline.
Although U.S. stocks stabilised overnight, with the Dow industrials rising 108.70 points, or 1.41 percent, to 7,803.36, analysts said there could be a further correction.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting body is due to meet later on Tuesday and while interest rates are expected to remain unchanged -- which would normally give share prices a lift -- analysts said it was already priced into the market.

"If the U.S holds above 7,700 points, that should be good news for Hong Kong market. Otherwise, it looks like it is due for a 10 percent correction from there. If the U.S. starts to correct further that is bad news," said Chen.

He said the Hang Seng Index should find support around 15,300 points. "If the market cannot hold around 15,300, then it is probably going for deeper correction and the target will be 14,000," said Chen. "14,000 would be a good level to buy."
